title: Primitive Data Types
description: The eight built-in types, the four you will actually use, and how to pick one.

content.value: Every Java variable states its type. That lets Java check your code before it runs, and know how much memory each box needs.
Java has eight built-in **primitive types**: the simplest pieces a value can be made of. Four cover almost everything you will write.

content.caption: You wrote `4.50` but Java printed `4.5`. A `double` stores the number, not how you typed it.

content.title: Four boxes, four types
content.caption: Each box only accepts its own kind of value.

items.text: `int`: whole numbers, about minus 2 billion to plus 2 billion.
`long`: bigger whole numbers. The value ends in `L`.
items.sub: Leave out the L and you get `integer number too large`.
Prices, averages, measurements. Java's default for decimals.

items.text: `float`: a smaller, older decimal type. The value ends in `f`.

content.caption: The last line: a `double` is not perfectly exact. Real programs use a different type for exact money, in Module 10.

items.title: int
items.text: If you would never want half of one, use `int`.

items.title: double
items.text: If it can have a fractional part, use `double`.

content.question: Which type should hold the number 8100000000?
content.explain: It is a whole number, but too big for an `int`. A `long` holds it, with an `L` on the end.

items.sub: Lower case, no quotes. It answers a yes or no question.

items.text: `char`: exactly one character in single quotes.

items.title: Compiles
items.text: Lower case `true`. One character in single quotes.

items.title: Error
items.text: `"true"` is text. `True` is wrong case. Double quotes are not a char. A char holds one character.

content.caption: Booleans drive every decision in Module 4. For a whole word you need `String`, the next lesson.

content.question: Which line compiles?
content.explain: Booleans are lower case with no quotes. A char holds just one character.

steps.note: A count of items: a whole number, so `int`.
Money needs decimals, so `double`. It stores 45.5.
In stock or not: a yes or no, so `boolean`.
One size letter: `char`, in single quotes.
The double prints without its trailing zero.
A boolean prints as the word `true`.

content.title: One shop item, the right type for each value

content.value: The other primitives, `long`, `float`, `short` and `byte`, are for when size matters. Until then, `int` and `double` are the right defaults.

practice.question: Declare one variable of each of the four main types to describe a book: an `int` for pages, a `double` for price, a `boolean` for whether you have read it, and a `char` for its shelf letter. Print all four with labels.
This program has three type mistakes. Run it, read each error, and fix them one at a time.
Print the result of `0.1 + 0.2` and see the surprise for yourself. Then print `1.0 / 3.0` as well.

quiz.question: Which type would you use for the number of students in a class?
options: int, because it is a whole count
double, because numbers are usually decimals
quiz.explain: You would never have half a student, so a whole number type is right. `int` covers counts up to about two billion.

quiz.question: Which type holds a price like 249.99?
quiz.explain: An `int` cannot hold a decimal point, so the fractional part would be lost. `double` is the normal choice for a number with decimals.

quiz.question: Which of these is a valid `boolean` value in Java?
quiz.explain: A boolean is `true` or `false`, in lower case and without quotes. With quotes it is text; with a capital letter it is a name Java does not know.

quiz.question: What is the difference between `'A'` and `"A"`?
options: `'A'` is a char (one character) and `"A"` is text.
There is no difference in Java.
`'A'` is text and `"A"` is a char.
quiz.explain: Single quotes make a `char`, which holds exactly one character. Double quotes make a `String`, which can hold any amount of text.

quiz.question: Why does `long worldPopulation = 8100000000;` fail to compile?
options: The number is read as an int first, so it needs an `L` on the end.
`long` is not a real Java type.
Variable names cannot be that long.
quiz.explain: Java treats plain digits as an `int` before looking at the type on the left. Writing `8100000000L` tells it the value is a `long`.
